articles.title: Anthony Mackie’s Dodging Questions About Doomsday Spoilers, But I’m Obsessed With His New Marvel Catchphrase
articles.summary: Captain America has found a new favorite phrase.
articles.content:
Anthony Mackie seems to have figured out how to get through an Avengers: Doomsday interview without giving Marvel's security team a heart attack. Whenever someone asks him about the upcoming Marvel movie , he just starts playing with the title. It was funny the first time. Now that he's doing it again, I'm beginning to think the MCU's Captain America has found his new catchphrase.

I don't know that Jean Grey actually destroyed an entire planet in the Fox X-Men movies , but I appreciate the former Falcon’s commitment to making the comparison sound terrifying. And considering Wanda's history in WandaVision and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , I understand why he'd reach for another famously powerful mutant. What he doesn't explain is how Sam Wilson and the other Avengers plan to deal with any of it.

The interviewer followed up by asking if he was really claiming he had no idea about Wanda's return. That's when Mackie delivered the line I've now decided needs to be printed on a shirt:

This is becoming a pattern. Mackie essentially gave the same answer to gave Josh Horowitz on Happy Sad Confused , describing the movie as a day full of a lot of, shall we say, fucking Doom. Now he's refined the joke into a cleaner line he can use in just about any interview. I hope he keeps going.

I love watching Anthony Mackie navigate all this. With Robert Downey Jr. returning to Marvel as Doctor Doom and so many heroes converging for the next Avengers movie, fans have plenty of questions. Mackie has apparently decided the title will answer most of them.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 Rotten Tomatoes Score Is a Franchise Low, But It's Not Bad News At All
articles.summary: Blade Runner 2099 officially arrives on Prime Video this week. Set 50 years after Denis Villeneuve’s sequel to Ridley Scott’s 1982 classic, the new series is set to offer audiences a whole new chapter in the story and one that flips the script just a bit where it’s now Replicants who are the majority while […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Blade Runner 2099 officially arrives on Prime Video this week. Set 50 years after Denis Villeneuve’s sequel to Ridley Scott’s 1982 classic, the new series is set to offer audiences a whole new chapter in the story and one that flips the script just a bit where it’s now Replicants who are the majority while humans are the minority. It’s a fresh take on things and now, the series’ Rotten Tomato score is out to show how it stacks up, but while Blade Runner 2099 is a franchise low, it’s actually not bad news at all for the cyberpunk world.

At the time of this article’s writing, Blade Runner 2099 has a Rotten Tomatoes score of 73%. That is around 15% lower than Blade Runner 2049 and 16% lower than Blade Runner . While this puts Blade Runner 2099 at a franchise low, 73% is still a respectable score, especially when you look at what the reviews are actually saying. Generally, most reviews agree that the new series very much understands the movies that came before it and just builds on things, expanding on the overall world and lore. There is also praise for both series stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer. While there are critiques that the series relies a bit too much on its aesthetics, that is almost to be expected considering how specific the world of Blade Runner really is.

What is particularly interesting about the reviews for Blade Runner 2099 and their discussion about the series’ aesthetics is that trailers for the series have already shown us that the series also has a very distinctively different look and feel . Notably, the series appears to be set against a more sunny landscape, which differs from the rainy world of Blade Runner . Mix that with the Replicant forward story and you have something that is, by design, not quite like what came before. If the reviews for the series are comparing Blade Runner 2099 to its predecessors and finding it measuring just a bit short, that honestly could bode well for how the series will be received by the metric that actually matters: the audience.

It is honestly not unusual for a movie or television series to land one way with critics only for the actual intended consumers of said entertainment to see it very differently. That honestly could be the case here. Critics could be positive, but subdued when it comes to their assessment of this new Blade Runner installment, but it could very well be the exact story from this beloved sci-fi franchise that fans have been wanting. After all, the idea of a future where Replicants are dominant is fascinating and tantalizing and does something that most fans generally want: offers something new with something already so beloved.

All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 drop on Prime Video November 25th.

articles.title: 22 Years Ago, Studio Ghibli's Most Whimsical Anti-War Movie Was Released & It Holds Up Even Today
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Studio Ghibli Howl's Moving Castle remains one of the most whimsical fantasies of all time, even 22 years after its premiere. Founded by directors Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata and producer Toshio Suzuki in 1985, Studio Ghibli eventually became one of the most globally renowned animation studios of all time. The films created under the banner of the studio […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Howl's Moving Castle remains one of the most whimsical fantasies of all time, even 22 years after its premiere. Founded by directors Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata and producer Toshio Suzuki in 1985,  Studio Ghibli  eventually became one of the most globally renowned animation studios of all time. The films created under the banner of the studio are known for captivating storytelling, deep emotional impact, visually striking animation, and more. One of  Miyazaki’s most unforgettable works  is still  Howl’s Moving Castle , a fantasy film based on Diana Wynne Jones’ 1986 novel.

The acclaimed film was even nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 78th Academy Awards. While fans have always debated over which is the best Ghibli film, there's no denying that when it comes to fantasy themes and anti-war allegory, Howl's Moving Castle stands out as the best among all of the studio's previous works. It's also a widely accepted opinion that the movie was even better than the original novel , which isn't something fans are used to seeing. The movie hit the Japanese theatres on November 20th, 2004, and its legacy remains unmatched even today.

The story centers around Sophie, a young girl who encounters the famous wizard Howl and catches the eye of an evil witch. Fueled by jealousy, the Witch of the Waste curses Sophie to turn into a 90-year-old woman. She accepts her fate, and Sophie leaves her home without telling anyone so she wouldn't end up being a burden to her family. She travels alone without any destination in mind and luckily manages to enter Howl’s Castle without an invitation. She begins working there as a maid, forming an unlikely bond with the residents, including Howl, as she gets entangled in the world of magic.

However, while the film presents itself as a romance fantasy, it's celebrated even to this day due to its anti-war allegory, themes of pacifism, self-acceptance, and many layers of core themes that will make you want to rewatch this beloved classic again and again . Miyazaki is widely recognized as a pacifist, and his ideologies are often reflected in his movies. Howl's Moving Castle portrays war without clearly showing any side as good or evil, and yet the senseless conflict continues to affect the lives of ordinary citizens.

Without any side to root for or any moral justification behind the war, the movie primarily focused on the brutalities of the war rather than showing a heroic tale. The people carried on with their lives despite the bombings as they became almost numb to the never-ending conflict. However, the most brutal depiction of the war was when Howl slowly began to lose his humanity after being forced to participate in the war. As a talented magician, he was forced to use his powers to cause destruction, which slowly made him turn into a monster. This is what sets the movie apart from other tales of war, and it's the reason why it's a timeless classic.

Has Howl's Moving Castle stayed with you ever since you watched it? Which moment do you find yourself thinking about the most? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Officially Renewed for Season 4 at Prime Video, But What's the Story?
articles.summary: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has been fighting an uphill battle since its conception, but has claimed many victories on its way to its current Season 3 run. As the finale episodes of The Rings of Power Season 3 premiere (at the time of writing this), Amazon Prime Video is wasting […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has been fighting an uphill battle since its conception, but has claimed many victories on its way to its current Season 3 run. As the finale episodes of The Rings of Power Season 3 premiere (at the time of writing this), Amazon Prime Video is wasting no time letting fans know that the journey will continue: The Rings of Power has officially been renewed for Season 4.

In addition to making a big announcement about Season 4 being confirmed, The Rings of Power also dropped an epic-looking announcement trailer for the next season, featuring the main players of Sauron (Charlie Vickers), Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), Gandalf (Daniel Weyman), During IV (Owain Arthur), and Pharazôn (Tyrstan Gravelle) all looking they are ready to throw down in the war for Middle-earth!

In the press announcement, Amazon Prime Video confirms that The Rings of Power Season 4 "is in pre-production and will begin filming this spring in the series' production home at Shepperton Studios in the UK."

The network also touted some numbers to show that Season 3 is continuing the show's growth and impact, grabbing "33 million viewers worldwide through its first 12 days, also ranking among the Top 10 most-watched returning seasons ever. Since S3's launch, The Rings of Power has maintained the #1 title worldwide on Prime Video, hitting #1 in 100+ countries. The Rings of Power continues to be one of the biggest entertainment drivers for new Prime membership sign-ups for Amazon, and the award-winning series has been watched by over 200 million viewers globally."

In a bold move, Amazon doesn't hold back about spoiling the finale of The Rings of Power Season 3, in order to explain what we're going to get in Season 4. ( SPOILERS! ) Season 3 will end with Sauron forging The One Ring that controls all the other Rings of Power given to Elves, Dwarves, and Men. The show stretched Sauron's struggle to create the One Ring into a seasonal arc that dovetails with the Elves and their attempts to both hold back Sauron's advancing darkness while protecting their forging secrets.

Obviously, the good guys failed on both counts. Season 4 of The Rings of Power will now cover the portion of J.R.R. Tolkein's lore where Sauron uses the power of the One Ring to go to war against the Elves and the kingdom of Númenór. Given the five-year jump in time between Seasons 2 and 3, it wouldn't be surprising if Season 4 plunges us into the midst of that war, when the fate of Middle-earth takes a pivotal turn when Sauron chooses a new tactic to break his enemy's might. At this point, it feels like Season 4's finale would be the "Fall of Númenór," while Season 5 would end the show with the "War of the Last Alliance," in which Sauron has the One Ring cut from his finger, destroying his physical form and bringing the Second Age of Middle-earth to an end, and seeding events for both The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings . That would fulfill Amazon's original 5-season plan for The Rings of Power perfectly.

" The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has become a defining series for Prime Video,” Peter Friedlander, Head of Global Television, Amazon MGM Studios, said in his statement. “As Season 3 delivers the landmark moment fans have been waiting for — the forging of the One Ring — we are proud to confirm Season Four with J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay, and the entire creative team. We look forward to bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien's Second Age."

articles.title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Creating Glenn Close’s Over-the-Top Looks by Leaning Into Drusilla’s ‘Narcissist’ Nature
articles.summary: Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you're Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of […]
articles.content:
Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you're Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in "The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping."

In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins' best-selling prequel novel to the screen. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Adam's Law' Enjoys Early TV-Ratings Judgment at CBS Tony Awards Will Remain on CBS Through 2032 Under New Five-Year Deal

One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.

“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety .

And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

The character's Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close's skin back, creating a distorted appearance. She later added tabs on the sides of Close’s face to complete the illusion, along with fake teeth that heightened Drusilla’s “scary” and “eerie” appearance. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“[Glenn] really wanted to pull it so taut that it changed all of her facial features, which it really did,” Spencer tells Variety .

Daigeler and Spencer's shared mission: to create visuals that resonate with the franchise’s devoted fans — who “know their stuff inside out,” Spencer quips. "They're so passionate." When the book was released and casting announcements began rolling out, Spencer would regularly check social media to see what fans envisioned for the adaptation and what details they hoped to see on screen.

Below, Spencer and Daigeler break down the process of creating each of Drusilla’s costumes, hair and makeup, as well as the inspiration behind each look.

Drusilla makes her grand entrance at the District 12 reaping, wheeled into the frame wearing a bold yellow ensemble. The outfit is a stark contrast to the muted colors worn throughout Panem’s poorest district — the exact irony Spencer and Daigeler hoped to portray by making that the character's brightest look in the film.

"It shouldn’t have any practicality. That is why she was driven in," Daigeler says of the tightly-cinched yellow coat dress. "It was supposed to be very stiff."

To complement the dress’ high collar, Spencer styled Close with an orange bob that also paid homage to the film’s ‘70s aesthetic. At Close's request, the look was completed with a raven headpiece — which, to be clear, was not an intentional nod to Lenore Dove’s name poem.

“For me, that sort of represents the children of the district — something that's taxidermied and dead on their head,” Spencer says about the headpiece. “And [Drusilla’s] so proud of that statement.”

Black medals and military-inspired shoulder plates further accentuated the ensemble, reinforcing Drusilla’s self-appointed authority. "She looked like a yellow general," Daigeler adds.

When representing District 12 at the Capitol’s chariot parade, Drusilla’s color palette dims to an all-black look that publicly links her to the district’s coal-mining industry. To elevate the outfit and solidify her Capitol status, Daigeler experimented with different textures to create the illusion of leather-like skin while also keeping her gold medals and fringed military epaulets. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“We wanted to give it strength,” Daigeler says of the outfit, which, she notes, also signals that things are getting more serious in the film's storyline. “We wanted it to be a little bit aggressive and very demanding. And very Capitol.”

Close initially wanted to style the look with an extravagant, fluffy hat, but she and Spencer ultimately settled on a simpler black wig with pointed horns so as not to distract from Drusilla’s face. The shorter bangs draw more attention to the exaggerated eye makeup and the face-slimming tabs.

Drusilla settles on a softer green dress for the tributes’ interviews with Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), which once again challenged Daigeler to maintain the character’s threads between outfit changes.

“Where’s the strength? Where’s the craziness?” she asked herself when accessorizing Drusilla’s third look, a crepey, olive-hued gown with a high neck and massive, billowy sleeves.

This time, Daigeler forwent Drusilla's medallions and instead made a statement by adding red gloves, tights and boots, paired with spiky necklaces.

Spencer leaned further into the softer ensemble by adding a wave to Drusilla’s hair, washed with a light shade of pink. "I really like fabrics and the colors and how the hair and makeup is going to be one big look altogether," Spencer notes.

Drusilla’s final appearance comes after Haymitch is declared the victor of the 50th Hunger Games — or, at least in Drusilla’s mind, after she is declared the victor. Complete with a purple sash, the look was designed to make it seem as though Drusilla herself had won the games.

This was the only outfit not described in Collins’ novel, giving Daigeler the creative freedom to execute her own vision. Knowing Drusilla would appear on the colorful stage, she wanted to put her in a bold red ensemble that would ensure she stood out.

Without a predetermined silhouette in mind, Daigeler drew inspiration from designers Alexander McQueen, Talyano and Balenciaga, as well as Renaissance-era shapes.

“I went to a beautiful fabric store in London, and I just found all these beautiful, different textured red fabrics,” Daigeler says. “I didn’t have it clear what would be the silhouette of the dress, but I knew that it should be an evening gown and somehow huge and over the top.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Spencer completed the transformation by leaning into the showgirl-inspired makeup, settling on a bright red lip and feathered hair.

"[Drusilla's] like a performer. When you really do think about it, she’s a narcissist. 'This is me. I’m bold. I’m dominant,'" Spencer says. "We had all the showgirls — all of those big colors and the feathers and everything else, so it's almost like a carnival of entertainers coming together on the stage. The set design, the colors, all the background people in the crowd are so, so important. What you’re portraying is a performance. It’s entertainment, and that’s who they are."

articles.title: Path of Exile 2's New Classes Are Bringing Some Much-Needed Creativity to ARPG Combat
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Grinding Gear Games You know what gets me more excited than seeing a ridiculous damage number pop up on screen? Finding an entirely new way to make that number happen. Really, there's a special kind of magic when a developer introduces a mechanic that makes you stop and reconsider everything you thought you knew about building a character. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google You know what gets me more excited than seeing a ridiculous damage number pop up on screen? Finding an entirely new way to make that number happen. Really, there's a special kind of magic when a developer introduces a mechanic that makes you stop and reconsider everything you thought you knew about building a character. One weird addition is all it takes before you're theorycrafting some wonderfully unhinged combination that might turn out to be your next obsession. That is the sort of creativity I want more of the ARPG genre, and Grinding Gear Games giving us all plenty of reasons to be excited about what comes next for Path of Exile 2 , starting with their upcoming 1.0 release .

The upcoming Shadow and Duelist classes are exactly the sort of additions that make me want to drop everything and start experimenting. The Shadow wants to turn combat into an elaborate game of cat and mouse. The Duelist looks ready to make swordplay an absolute playground of mechanical possibilities. Neither is content with simply handing players another collection of abilities or spells and calling it a day. Oh, no.They're introducing mechanics that could fundamentally change how people approach encounters, and the possibilities are downright exciting. Honestly, I love what this studio is doing.

Let's talk about the Shadow, because I absolutely love the idea of turning stealth into an actual combat identity in an ARPG. This isn't just a character who sneaks behind an enemy before delivering a slightly stronger backstab. The Shadow can remain concealed until monsters get close enough to detect them, creating opportunities to decide exactly when an encounter begins. Dagger skills become empowered while hidden, so there's a genuine incentive to strike from the darkness rather than immediately jumping into the fray. Then things get even more interesting with traps. You can prepare them while concealed before revealing yourself and triggering a sequence of detonations. Just imagine the sheer satisfaction of setting up an elaborate little death trap and watching an unsuspecting pack of monsters wander straight into it. It's wonderfully devious, and I can already picture players coming up with increasingly ridiculous ways to turn entire encounters into sushi the moment they start.

The Duelist, meanwhile, looks like an absolute treat for anyone who loves getting into the thick of combat. Swords are finally joining Path of Exile 2 's weapon roster, and GGG clearly isn't interested in making this a simple case of giving players another object to swing around. The new weapon type comes with its own stance system, allowing certain abilities to function differently depending on whether you're in Ready, Blood, or Sand Stance. Blood leans into bleeding enemies while Sand offers a different approach to dealing damage, giving sword users another layer of decision-making to explore. What I particularly enjoy about this design is how it encourages players to think about the relationship between their abilities rather than simply finding the biggest number and pressing the corresponding button until everything dies.

Here's what really gets me excited, though: these two classes couldn't be much more different. Both classes offer their own mechanical rabbit holes for players to disappear into, and I suspect the community is going to have an absolute field day figuring out what these classes can do. New classes in PoE 2 tend to come with a lot more than what they represent on the surface, and that's really where my excitement stems from.

There's a reason people can sink hundreds or even thousands of hours into ARPGs. Building a character is practically an obsession in its own right. You start with a vague idea of what you want to create, spend an unreasonable amount of time figuring out how to make it work, and eventually emerge with something that can turn an entire screen of enemies into a very brief memory. It's glorious. But I think the genre sometimes gets a little too comfortable with the idea that progression alone is enough to keep things exciting. Another passive node makes your character stronger. Another piece of equipment pushes your damage even higher. Fantastic! But what if the next update gave you an entirely new way to fight instead? That's the kind of progression that really gets my attention.

This is where Path of Exile 2 has the potential to become something special. GGG has spent development continually finding ways to push beyond familiar ARPG conventions, and the upcoming release represents a major opportunity to build on that foundation. The Shadow and Duelist are particularly exciting because their mechanics could inspire entirely new approaches to character building. Players are going to spend their time experimenting with trap combinations and discover how far they can push the Shadow's stealth mechanics. Duelist players will have their own mechanical playground to explore through. The real icing on the cake is that both classes add new mechanics, and since PoE 2 allows you to mix and match almost everything, the results are going to be spectacular. I wouldn't be surprised if some of the most interesting combinations emerge from players doing things GGG never expected. That's half the fun!

December 11 is an enormous milestone for Path of Exile 2 , but I'm just as interested in what the next few years could bring. The Shadow and Duelist already have me excited to see what GGG does next, and I absolutely love that the studio seems more interested in expanding what combat can be than simply giving us another way to make enemies explode. Although, to be fair, I'm certainly not opposed to making enemies explode.

Which of the new Path of Exile 2 mechanics has you most excited to experiment with when the full release arrives? Let us know in the comment section below.

articles.title: Cyclops May Have Saved the World, But His Sacrifice Could Be the X-Men's Worst Nightmare
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Cyclops is the one hero who has always been at the forefront of the X-Men's attempts to save the world, and he is most tenacious when he is defending mutants. This was put to the test in the new "DNX" storyline when Cyclops went alone to face the Chairman, who is the original Beast from […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Cyclops is the one hero who has always been at the forefront of the X-Men's attempts to save the world, and he is most tenacious when he is defending mutants. This was put to the test in the new "DNX" storyline when Cyclops went alone to face the Chairman, who is the original Beast from the first X-Men lineup. The Chairman worked with 3K to release the same disease that destroyed the world in the "Age of Revelation" timeline. His goal was to create mutants and destroy humans in the test area. What resulted was turning mutants into grotesque creatures and leaving the entire town a disaster area.

In DNX #5 by Jed MacKay and Federico Vicentini, Cyclops went to battle the Chairman and destroy all his equipment and machinery. However, this turned into a battle where the old friends realized that the only way they could win would be to kill each other. In the end, after one explosion, it was all over, with Cyclops seemingly sacrificing his life to stop the Chairman.

The entire finale of the "DNX" storyline was a personal one, as it kept flipping back to Cyclops and Beast when they first met after Hank McCoy joined the X-Men for the first time. This was then shown in conjunction with their massive battle, where Beast kept trying to claim he was in the right, and Cyclops was fighting to keep him from hurting anyone else. It was a personal battle, and it even seemed like Cyclops finally got through to Hank by the end, although the fight ended with an explosion that seemed to kill both of the original X-Men members.

When the explosion happened, it stopped the Chairman's plan, and it saved the world from any further danger from this chemical warfare that 3K had planned. However, this was also witnessed by the heroes on the outside of the containment bubble. The Fantastic Four and members of the X-Men were all there watching when it exploded. Reed Richards said it was a small explosion and that Cyclops had saved everyone by keeping the device from reaching critical mass. But the problem came when Kid Omega said that he couldn't reach Scott's mind anymore. The X-Men realized that Cyclops had died to save the world.

This seemed sad, but it then led the X-Men to quickly make new preparations. While Reed Richards didn't understand why Psylocke and the X-Men had to leave the decontamination and liaising with ONE to the Fantastic Four, Susan Richards said that they would deal with it, understanding there was something that the mutants had to deal with. While Beast was traumatized, realizing that it was another version of him who was responsible, Psylocke and the X-Men knew what was coming and what Cyclops' death means for the planet.

As the X-Men were leaving the scene, Psylocke said that Cyclops drilled into them what they had to do if he died. They had to get back to their base in Alaska and prepare because Jean Grey was coming. Not only was she coming, but with the full power of the Phoenix, Jean would want answers for the death of her husband. That last panel showed an angry and heartbroken Jean Grey, surrounded by the Phoenix Force, and it looks like Cyclops saved the planet, but his death might have created a brand-new threat with a devastated Phoenix.

There was a twist at the end that showed that neither the Chairman nor Cyclops was dead. There is no telling how far in the future this took place, and the location itself was redacted, but the Chairman woke up Cyclops and said they had both been sleeping long enough and they had work to do. That sets up a new mystery about whether the Chairman is still a villain or if he is going to try to make up for things. It also showed Cyclops without his visor on, and his pupils solid white. Why Kid Omega can't see Scott is also unknown.

However long in the future that epilogue takes place doesn't matter for now. What does matter is that Jean Grey is headed for Earth , and she is not happy knowing that Scott Summers has died. Jean left Earth, leaving Scott behind, to embrace her full role as the Phoenix and has been facing universal threats in deep space. articles.title: IATSE Reaches Tentative Agreement for Broadway Stagehands
articles.summary: However, the union said its Broadway wardrobe workers are still without a new contract and have voted to authorize a strike.
articles.content:
IATSE Local One, which represents stagehands on Broadway , has reached a tentative agreement with the Broadway League, ahead of the lucrative holiday weeks.

This comes after Local One members had voted to authorize a strike in October, after working on an expired contract since late July. If called, a work stoppage from Local One would have likely put a halt to most Broadway shows. The agreement still needs to be ratified by members of the union, with details of the tentative agreement planned to be available ahead of the union’s December meeting.

However, another local chapter of the union, IATSE Local 764, which represents Broadway dressers and others who work on costumes, still remains without a contract, and voted Sunday to authorize a strike if necessary.

Local 764 members have been bargaining with The Broadway League, a trade association for Broadway producers and general managers, since June. The members’ previous agreement had expired July 26. The League cancelled bargaining sessions scheduled for November 18 and 19, according to IATSE, and Local 764 has been pushing for new dates.

IATSE said the issues still in contention include wages and a gender pay gap that has existed for decades for Broadway wardrobe workers. The field is predominantly female, and has been paid “significantly lower rates than stagehand classifications historically held predominantly by men” according to the union, with Local 764 department heads needing to work 45 percent longer to earn pay comparable to workers in similar department-head roles.

Both Actors’ Equity and the American Federation of Musicians Local 802 also voted to authorize strikes last year, and came very close to doing so, before striking new contracts with the Broadway League.

articles.title: Alfonso Ribeiro on the "Wild" Ride of 'DWTS' Season 35, Reuniting With Tatyana Ali and Why He Won’t Compete in an All-Winners Season
articles.summary: To commemorate the finale of ‘DWTS,’ Ribeiro chats with THR about the ups-and-downs of season 35, his favorite part about hosting the show and why he can’t predict who will join him in the winners circle on Tuesday night.
articles.content:
Season 35 of Dancing With the Stars marks Alfonso Ribeiro ’s fifth season hosting the show, and he has no idea how it will end.

After winning season 19 with Witney Carson, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air joined the series as a co-host in its 31st season, a year that he believes laid the foundation for the show’s resurgence. “I think we owe a debt of gratitude to Charli D’Amelio doing the show. … Her being literally one of the most popular social media TikTok stars opened the door to an audience that previously didn’t care about this show,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter of what he pinpoints to DWTS ’ spike in popularity (and ratings ) in recent years. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County' Renewed at Hulu TV Lindsay Hubbard Teases 'Summer House' Spinoff 'In the City' Season 2: "Better Than Season One"

The TikTok star certainly brought new eyes to the series, but Ribeiro also refreshed it as host. After one year executing the job alongside Tyra Banks, Julianne Hough stepped in as his co-host, and the duo have remained at the post since. They both bring unique perspectives to DWTS: Ribeiro, as a celebrity who won the series, and Hough, as a former professional dancer and judge.

Ribeiro says there’s so many things that he loves about hosting the show, but one standout is the mentorship he’s able to offer the celebrities. This year, his Fresh Prince sister Tatyana Ali hit the ballroom floor, which he says has been “beautiful for me to experience with her.”

Ali is one of five couples still competing for a chance to win the Len Goodman mirrorball trophy on Tuesday night. Ribeiro admittedly doesn’t know what factors will hold more weight when determining this year’s winner.

“It is quite wild to me because this is a very different season than any other season we've ever had,” he says. “So, all of the normal things that we would be able to gauge doesn't really exist this year.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One thing Ribeiro hopes is that the portion of the audience spreading hate towards contestants will fade in future seasons. “At the end of the day, this is a dance competition show. This isn't life or death. No one's life is changing that greatly from this. It is designed for people to let loose, have some fun and truly enjoy these incredible celebrities,” he adds.

To commemorate the finale of DWTS , Ribeiro chats with THR below about the ups-and-downs of season 35; being in the ballroom and getting the chance to dance with Ali; his opinion on fans who believe celebrities with prior dance experience shouldn’t be cast on the show; and why you won’t ever see him compete on another All-Star (or all-winners) iteration of DWTS .

How does it feel to almost be at the finish line of season 35 of Dancing With the Stars ?

This is an incredibly epic season. The numbers, the fans and the interest has been through the roof. We feel really blessed to do something no other show has really ever done in history, which is come back from the brink of extinction to turn around and become the No. 1 show on television. We've got a great cast, and they've done an incredible job of opening themselves up and allowing America to get to know them. Deena Katz and Conrad Green put a great team together.

The season 35 finale is going to be airing live coast-to-coast for the first time. What do you think that says about the growth and reach of the show that this was so wanted by fans, but also so much so that the affiliates came to an agreement for this to happen? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That's a major move, right? The only thing on television that does that are sporting events, and the fact that we can move side by side with the NFL and NBA, and people are willing to, on a Tuesday night on the West Coast and Mountain time, come home a little early so that they could watch the show live is quite spectacular when you really think of it. That the affiliates and the network have that much trust in doing this as a finale says that they truly believe that this will work out great for the show and for the sponsors and the companies buying ad time. It says a lot about what they believe in the show.

Do you think that airing the finale live could be a potential test to see how the viewership comes in to see if the show would adapt this live format for a future season?

I can't really speak on it, obviously, because I don't know anyone's thoughts. Anything I say would be conjecture, not anything real. I actually believe that it works the way that it works so far. Of course, we'd love for everyone on the West Coast and everyone in the Mountain time zone to be able to vote for their favorites. I think the interesting way would be to do it on Disney+ and not necessarily on ABC. But the question becomes, does the audience truly support it? If the numbers end up being as good or better, then of course let's do it. But there are things that would severely be hampered by that. Technically speaking, ABC News Tonight is the No. 1 broadcast show on Tuesday nights, so you'd be giving up on that for the success of Dancing . The smarter people will make that decision, and we'll see where that leads us. We're super excited that we're getting to experience this particular case. Hopefully all of America and everybody on the West Coast watches it live and we break ratings and voting records.

Tatyana has had such an incredible journey. What has it been like being able to be there and be a part of that journey?

I've been trying to get her to do the show for many years, and the timing just wasn't right. And so happy she did, and really, mostly, so happy for her. It isn't about me; it's about her and what she is getting to experience. The little girl I met in 1990, [she’s] all grown up. She's such a special person. What this show did for me was show America who Alfonso really was, not that character [from Fresh Prince ]; same situation for her: getting to experience who Tatyana Ali is and people falling in love with the beautiful human she is.

What was your reaction when she came to you with the idea for you to be a part of her Dedication Night dance in honor of James [Avery]?

It started obviously with the producers asking me the question first. When we finally talked about it, it was already a yes. I expressed my very small concerns of, does that make it look like I'm favoring someone over everyone else, and will that be something that we ultimately have to deal with? And everyone came to the conclusion that that wouldn't be an issue. The thing that took it over the top for me was that the dedication was to James Avery, and it was bigger than just this show. James Avery played my dad on three different shows, so dedicating it to him felt so right. It was a great opportunity for us to spend extra time together and go through the process of doing a competitive number on the show. I dance all the time on the show, but to be part of a competitive number made it extra special. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

You have seen the growth the show has had in the past few years. What do you think it has been about these past two seasons that have really hooked a wider audience and opened the show up to more people?

I actually think it goes back further than the last two seasons. I think we owe a debt of gratitude to Charli D’Amelio for doing the show. Before her season, it was always an older audience. It wasn't what it is today, and I think that her being literally one of the most popular social media TikTok stars opened the door to an audience that previously didn't care about this show and always looked at it as, Oh, that's my grandmother's show. That's my parents' show . It wasn't their show, and I think Charli D’Amelio made it OK for it to be their show. As the years went along, it just grew and grew, and more people talked about it, and it became this very cool energy that moved through the younger generation. Back in the day, we used to have this term, the “water cooler” TV shows, where people would stand around the water cooler at the office and talk about the show. Well, social media has become the water cooler, and this show has gained on that.

It's beautiful to watch how the young audience is falling in love with the show. I certainly do hope that the younger audience can be fickle, and know as quickly as they fall in love with something, they fall out of love with it. I'm hoping that they stay in love with it for a while, and recognize that what we're trying to do is bring love and joy to an audience. I will say that the audience out there that adds a lot of hate, negativity and bullying — I hope that goes away and it becomes more of just love and joy. At the end of the day, this is a dance competition show. This isn't life or death. No one's life is changing that greatly from this. It is designed for people to let loose, have some fun and truly enjoy these incredible celebrities. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

There has been a lot of chatter and conversation online this season. Has there been one specific conversation online that has specifically stood out to you?

No, I'm not going to say anything specific. What I will say is everyone is entitled to their perspective of what they think the show is, and I would say that for me, it isn't necessarily a show about people who have no dance experience learning to dance. You do that in Hollywood, it becomes a really short list of people. I look at this show as this is just a bunch of celebrities coming together to learn ballroom dancing. Whether they start with a lot of experience or they start with zero experience, it's about the journey that they all go on.

What is your favorite part about hosting Dancing With the Stars ?

I really do love being almost a mentor to a lot of our celebrities. I go in on Monday and I'm there all day watching every one of the performances and being there as a support system; I'm there for all of it. I've been the host of the show, [this year] being my fifth season, and yes, I was a contestant, but I was also a fan from season one on, so I've watched almost every person that's ever done this show in all 35 seasons. That's really the part that I enjoy: I enjoy being there for them, and it's a gift that I get to be a part of their journey in some form.

Do you have a favorite number you performed on the show?

My favorite was my Paso Doble to “Turn Down for What.” That was my all-time favorite one. It was a lot of fun to do that. I mean, the music — songs make dances, and you would never think [of doing] a Paso Doble to that song, but yet Witney choreographed a great number having Lindsay [Arnold] on it with us. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Evans also recalled a dinner with Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and co-president Louis D’Esposito while the team was still filming “Endgame.” The topic of playing Nomad, Steve’s alternate identity after giving up the Captain America title, came up.

The Broadway League and IATSE Local One of theater workers have reached a tentative deal to avoid a strike that could have disrupted the lucrative holiday season. The agreement is pending ratification by union members.

articles.title: GTA 6 Analysis Says the Game Plays Better on Xbox Than PS5
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games There are many features to praise in Grand Theft Auto 6, with the game easily being one of the most celebrated in the last decade, but the PlayStation 5 version of the title isn't without problems. While Xbox Series X|S players of GTA 6 aren't reporting any big performance issues, those on the PS5 version […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are many features to praise in Grand Theft Auto 6 , with the game easily being one of the most celebrated in the last decade, but the PlayStation 5 version of the title isn't without problems. While Xbox Series X|S players of GTA 6 aren't reporting any big performance issues, those on the PS5 version can tell that frame rates for the game are lacking in some areas. While the PS5 Pro almost eliminates all of these complaints, those without an enhanced edition of the PlayStation 5 console could be left in the dark about why their game isn't quite acting like it should be.

In the grand scheme of things, the differences between the Xbox and PS5 editions of GTA 6 are minimal, as they come down to individual console hardware limitations rather than the content of the game. Players on either device can experience the full breadth of GTA 6 with zero changes between versions, engaging with the same innovative world and story that has garnered many positive reviews in the short time since the game's launch. Yet, those who want their time with GTA 6 to be 100% perfect, the PS5 might be the place to pursue that goal.

A large amount of research conducted by Digital Foundry has tested the performance of GTA 6 on the PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and the Xbox Series X|S through challenging situations. Digital Foundry put each console through the ringer, testing the game's performance during highly chaotic segments where there was a lot going on in-game, such as big shootouts with police or driving through dense traffic at full speed. The game's ability to render and display areas, characters, events, encounters, and other information was solid across the board, but the PS5 lacked in overall frames per second.

Frame consistency is the biggest issue with the PS5, with GTA 6 sometimes struggling to deliver 30 FPS on the console compared to the much smoother Xbox Series X|S. Large, crowded areas tend to cause a few frame dips on the PS5's end, usually in unpredictable ways that are noticeable, but hard to pin down exactly. This can lead to player frustration easily, especially since there isn't a particular area, story segment, or other factor to avoid that causes this problem. Thankfully, GTA 6 doesn't use continual detail systems in-game, creating a balance on PS5 that doesn't allow frames to dip too harshly.

For those curious, the video below has the entire breakdown of the PS5/Series X|S showdown from Digital Foundry:

Most players likely won't be too bothered by this issue, as the shadows and lighting of the PS5 version still are of high quality. That being said, the PS5 edition of GTA 6 doesn't ray trace any shadows, creating slight visual dips when you're looking other versions of the game side by side. Instead, ray traced shadows are mimicked on the PS5, using an advanced shadow map solution that makes it seem like ray tracing is in effect during varied lightning effects within gameplay. This becomes obvious in reflections throughout GTA 6 , whether in a mirror or water you can see images in.

Despite these pitfalls, overall image quality on PS5 is still good for GTA 6 as a whole. The only problem is within the inconsistencies that the Xbox Series X|S simply doesn't have, as the aforementioned shadow and reflection limitations aren't as noticeable in a more stable 30 FPS environment. 4K sharpness also just isn't consistent at all on the PS5, as its already apparent visual struggles prevent it from achieving that level of smoothness. Rapid camera movements, explosives, and other big clutter on screen make the PS5's shortcomings easier to identify, through they shouldn't be a deal-breaker in most cases.

Even though the base PS5 has FPS struggles, the Xbox Series X|S's visual consistencies don't match up to the PS5 Pro's depiction of GTA 6 . The PS5 Pro actually has ray tracing and visual upgrades, therefore eliminating some of the factors that cause frame drops in the main version of GTA 6 on the PS5. 4K upscaling also makes visuals much smoother, keeping a continual 30 FPS with little to no issues at any point of gameplay. Even during cluttered moments, the PS5 Pro operates excellently, even rendering details at far distances with better clarity than either the PS5 or Series X|S.

Higher resolution reflections allow the game to lock in at 30 FPS, even if players desire to unlock GTA 6 into 40 FPS or even 60 once it arrives on PC. For now, the research points toward the console that, unsurprisingly, was designed to have the best experience possible for the highly anticipated Rockstar game from the ground up. The stability of the PlayStation 5 Pro makes up for the struggles of the base PS5 somewhat, but unfortunately, the majority of players will be on the frame dropping version of the console as the Xbox Series X|S beats it out in terms of performance.

What console are you playing GTA 6 on? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: I Get Why Red Rising Fans Want Joseph Zada To Play A Certain Gold, But Wait A Second
articles.summary: The Hunger Games star should obviously play a Gold... but which one?
articles.content:
Now that we know that a Red Rising movie is in the works, it's completely understandable that we'd be on the edges of our seats waiting for any word on who might be cast in the book-to-screen adaptation . Eagle-eyed Red Rising fans -- yes, that's an intentional nod to the Bellona sigil right there -- have picked up on the fact that author Pierce Brown has followed Joseph Zada on Instagram, which has led to a lot of enthusiastic speculation that the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping star might be in talks to play a role in Red Rising movie. I've seen one specific character name coming up a lot as the perfect role for Zada to take on, but wait a second, because there are options here.

On the other hand, the fact that Pierce Brown and Francis Lawrence have known each other for years ( per Lawrence ) also needs to be acknowledged, as Brown could've met Zada through the director and followed him just to follow him... as people do. In short, the follow could mean nothing or it could mean something.

The handsome Bellona's name came up quite a bit in the comments discussing who Zada should play, and I get it. Even as Golds go, Cassius is known to be extremely handsome, and well, Zada fits that description. Zada's also got the blond curls , which is one of the most distinctive things about Cassius' looks. Also, as a Gold, Cassius is tall, and so is Zada.

When it comes to casting the Gold characters (and Obsidians) in the movie, it seems unlikely that they're going to find the perfect actors to play the roles, who also just so happen to be around or above seven feet tall. How they make the size differences among the colors stand out on screen is going to be a challenge by itself, whether they use forced perspective, special effects or other techniques. Still, if they want to cast actors on the taller side for the Golds, IMDB has Zada listed as 6'2".

Darrow's the other name I've seen circulating, and honestly, he's the first person I thought of when I saw the topic of Joseph Zada possibly starring in the Red Rising movie. Maybe it's seeing him play a District 12 kid in Sunrise on the Reaping that makes it easier for me to envision him as a lowRed with a score to settle. There are a lot of sides to Darrow, especially when we factor in the teen that he is at the start of Red Rising , and the transition (and drama) he goes through in the first book. I can see Zada tackling that arc really well.

Nah. I can't even picture it... but it'd be fun to see his take on the role.

I'm going to cross Pax off the list right away. Even if Zada bulked up a lot for the part, I picture a guy with the size and personality of a jovial (or ferocious, when necessary) bear for the youngest Telemanus son. However, Roque would be an interesting option. I don't think Zada fits how I imagine Roque to look, but I do think he'd have an interesting take on the thoughtful character.

Hamilton was the top grossing show last week, rising back above $3 million as the industry neared its lucrative holiday week, followed by Other Desert Cities with $2.5 million and the Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell-led Much Ado About Nothing , which still brought in $2 million in a week that included its comped opening night performance.

The Lion King followed with $1.9 million and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child with $1.7 million.

Here There are Blueberries , a play about museum curators examining previously undiscovered photos from the Holocaust, cracked $1 million for the first time since beginning previews in early November. The show played to close to 100 percent capacity with an average ticket price of $128.

New musical Galileo saw a slight dip in capacity and grosses after lead actor Raúl Esparza missed performances from Nov. 16 through Nov. 18 while recovering from a concussion. Wanted, a new musical which opened Nov. 8, also saw a dip in capacity down to 85 percent, with the show grossing $661,143 across eight performances.

Broadway’s holiday fare has not yet taken off with consumers, with The Blue Man Group playing to 60 percent capacity, illusionist show Now You See Me playing to 77 percent capacity and radio play It’s a Wonderful Life playing to 76 percent.

articles.title: Stephen King Was Outed as Richard Bachman Thanks to This Book That Was Turned Into a Movie 30 Years Ago
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Paramount Pictures It has been 30 years since a movie came out based on the Stephen King novel that outed the author as Richard Bachman. When King was breaking into the novel industry, he found himself pigeonholed into the horror genre. With instant hits like Carrie, 'Salem's Lot, and The Shining, King was expected to keep writing […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It has been 30 years since a movie came out based on the Stephen King novel that outed the author as Richard Bachman. When King was breaking into the novel industry, he found himself pigeonholed into the horror genre. With instant hits like Carrie , ' Salem's Lot , and The Shining , King was expected to keep writing horror, but he wanted to try to write in other genres too. While he has mostly stuck with horror over his career, King is much more than that. As Richard Bachman, he released sci-fi ( The Running Man ), thrillers ( The Long Walk ), and even intense psychological dramas ( Roadwork ).

In 1984, King wrote a horror novel under the Richard Bachman pseudonym , and it quickly led to fans connecting the dots and realizing that King was Bachman. After he retired the Bachman pseudonym, the novel ended up being adapted into a movie. Thinner came out in theaters on October 25, 1996, and it gave movie fans a look at the story that King wrote behind his assumed identity.

Thinner Helped Reveal Stephen King's Pseudonym Image Courtesy of Paramount Pictures Most of King's novels under the name Richard Bachman were not horror stories, although they all had terrifying premises. Rage was a book about a high school student who killed two of his teachers and took his classmates hostage. The Running Man was about a deadly reality TV show , written years before reality TV was even a thing in real life. Roadwork was about a man barricading himself in his house to prevent the state from demolishing it to build a freeway. These are not the stories one might expect from the King of Horror. However, Thinner was exactly what people would expect from Stephen King.

Thinner follows an obese upper-class attorney named Billy Halleck who has a wife and daughter. He is not an ethical attorney and recently defended a mafia boss and got him acquitted of a murder charge. After celebrating the victory, he is involved in an accident while driving where he runs over an elderly Romani woman, killing her. He is acquitted of manslaughter in a case presided over by his friend, a judge, and thanks in part to the police chief committing perjury in the trial. However, he doesn't get away with it because the woman's father, Tadzu Lempke, places a curse on Billy on the steps of the courthouse.

What happens next is that Billy starts to lose weight rapidly despite not exercising or eating right. Billy soon learns that the judge and police chief were also cursed, with one becoming a lizard-like being and the other getting ulcers on his face and hands. They both die by suicide, but Billy fights to find a way to survive the curse, even as he begins to waste away. It was pure horror, with the morality tale carrying it to the end. The ending even has the double twist that King is best known for, where the seeming victory comes with a bitter defeat, and Billy realizes he will never escape the curse, one way or the other.

While King created an entire fictional biography for Richard Bachman, and even used a photo of one of his literary agent's friends, fans began to suspect the truth. Some began to send angry letters, accusing Bachman of copying King's style, while others began to wonder if Bachman was a pseudonym. This led to a bookstore employee in Washington, D.C., who was a huge King fan, discovering the truth. This man looked at the copyright documentation that tied things to King. He reached out to King, and then the author called him and admitted it before revealing it to the world and killing off his pseudonym.

Thinner remains an underseen Stephen King adaptation. Robert John Burke played Billy Halleck, but there were some more familiar faces in the cast. These included Joe Mantegna as the Mafia boss. It was also directed by a big-time director, Tom Holland, who had also directed the King miniseries The Langoliers and was the man who directed and co-wrote the original Child's Play movie and wrote and directed the cult vampire film Fright Night . However, Thinner wasn't reviewed well and did poorly at the box office.

However, there are other Richard Bachman adaptations that have been received more favorably, including two King movies released in 2025. The first Richard Bachman adaptation was The Running Man in 1987, an Arnold Schwarzenegger movie in which he starred as a man forced to play a deadly game on reality television for his freedom. That is also where Bachman's books are becoming popular again. In 2025, The Running Man was remade, and a second Bachman story, The Long Walk , was released after years of fans demanding its arrival on the big screen. If anything, it proves what King wanted fans to know. He was more than just horror, even if it was a horror story that outed his secret.

Sonny Liston stood 6'1″ and, in his prime, weighed in at 218 pounds. For Prime Video 's The Greatest , actor Amin Joseph ( Snowfall ) added the requisite 23 pounds to his 6'1 (and ½"!) frame to perfectly match that of the former champ.

Joseph proved to be a solid facsimile of Liston in other ways, too. For one, he can really throw hands.

"I grew up fighting," Joseph told The Hollywood Reporter . "My dad got me into boxing when I was probably around 8 or 9."

It was probably no coincidence that the formal lessons began shortly after the family moved to Harlem. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Deborah Ann Woll to Reprise 'God of War' Role in Prime Video Series TV Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up

Either way, it stuck, and Joseph would box on and off into his college years studying theatre at Howard University. The natural southpaw (not that he told production before landing the role — Liston was a righty) says he had a "knack" for the violent sport, but ultimately was unwilling or unable to "slave [his] mind over" to a coach.

"If he says, 'Run through a wall.' If he says, 'Eat sheetrock' — you need to slave your mind over to that process," Joseph said. "[My coach] saw that I already had self-confidence and that I was already shaped as a young man in a certain way, and it was just not worth the investment (for him)."

Boxing is a sport built on length, speed, power, mental fortitude, and in many cases, having an absent (or at least shitty) father. With a present dad at home, Joseph was not looking for what so many younger fighters subconsciously seek. His training had logical limits.

"If [a trainer says], 'Run at 3 in the morning when it's raining,' you don't need someone going, 'Well, wait a minute — is that the smartest thing?'" Joseph explained. "You need someone that goes, 'I'm running.' Because it could be life or death if you're in the ring and [a coach] says, 'I need you to throw this combo.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The coach needs the fighter to throw that combo and never question his corner. Joseph, who describes himself as "a thespian through and through," always saw past the ring.

Liston, for better or worse, was a boxing coach's dream. Born into a poor sharecropping family, Liston was uneducated and basically tortured by his father. As a young teenager, he ran away from their Arkansas plantation and toward the streets of St. Louis, Missouri. By his early 20s (Liston never really knew his age), Liston was incarcerated.

Not that he minded much: inmates get three meals a day, every single day.

Liston "wanted to be accepted" like "a child" does, Joseph said. So he did as he was told. It was not a lifetime of great advice.

It was in the Missouri State Penitentiary that Liston found boxing. Or really, it was boxing that found Liston. Once more, that would be for better (he'd become World Heavyweight Champion in 1962) and for worse (Liston died under suspicious circumstances in 1970). Throughout his career, Liston was surrounded by unsavory characters.

Before reading Ben Watkins' scripts, Joseph didn't know more about Liston than your average… Joseph. He was tangentially aware of the man from the below-pictured infamous KO, which lived on as a mural on the wall of Joseph's boxing gym (and surely hundreds of others).

Joseph got the education needed from those scripts. He also gained the confidence that he'd have the appropriate screen time to show Liston's "thought process," as well as his "humility" and "humbleness." It is Joseph's quietest moments in the series that speak the loudest to viewers — not an easy task when playing opposite the loudest and most relentless talker in boxing history. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

(Cassius Clay/Muhammad Ali was portrayed with trademark bravado by Jaalen Best. Yes, "Best" was "The Greatest" in what THR TV critic Daniel Fienberg called "a star-making performance." Fienberg said Joseph "makes Liston into a flawed but tragic figure, ferocious in the ring but eager to find acceptance outside of it," and calls Liston/Joseph's talk show-appearance scene "one of the series’ highlights.")

As heavy as Joseph's new (pure muscle) weight was, what weighed most on the real Liston was "the shame" of being illiterate throughout adulthood, Joseph said. For Joseph, the greatest selling point of The Greatest is that Watkins doesn't portray Liston as "a dimwit," as the media of the time certainly did.

"Literacy isn't a direct correlation to your intelligence," Joseph said. "[Liston] is a man that moves in the silence, but when he does talk, it's so poignant."

Inter Alia, the previewing production of Suzie Miller's new play starring Rosamund Pike, seems about to repeat its London success here on Broadway , with the first seven-performance week selling out and grossing $993,103 .

The play (opening at the Music Box Theatre on December 1) was one of the stronger performers on Broadway for the week ending November 22, along with other sell-outs A Few Good Men, Hamilton, Much Ado About Nothing , Other Desert Cities and, in its final week, The Imaginary Invalid starring Bill Irwin (grossing $599,290 ).

Top earner was, far and away, Hamilton , with Christopher Jackson back in the role of George Washington (through January 3), sending box office soaring to $3,039,502 . Closest runner up was Other Desert Cities at $2,562,632 . articles.title: Marvel Confirms Patrick Stewart Was Offered a Role in Avengers: Secret Wars
articles.summary: Marvel Avengers: Doomsday will be a major Marvel movie milestone in so many ways, and not all of them will be fantastical; some of them will be heartbreaking in a very real and painful way. For a long time, we thought that one of the biggest tugs on our heartstrings would be seeing actors Patrick Stewart […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday will be a major Marvel movie milestone in so many ways, and not all of them will be fantastical; some of them will be heartbreaking in a very real and painful way. For a long time, we thought that one of the biggest tugs on our heartstrings would be seeing actors Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen onscreen together as X-Men's Professor X and Magneto, one last time. However, the recent death of Patrick Stewart has changed that fundamentally, as Avengers: Doomsday will now serve as Stewart's final screen performance .

With Patrick Stewart gone, obviously his version of Charles Xavier will also end with Avengers: Doomsday . But apparently that wasn't the case originally.

Marvel Studios offered Stewart a role in Avengers: Secret Wars , seeing Xavier as the unwavering "conscience" guiding the heroes through the multiversal war, according to director Joe Russo. However, it was Stewart who turned down the offer, preferring to have a role only in Avengers: Doomsday .

Based on Joe Russo's full description, it doesn't sound like Xavier will have a big role in Avengers: Doomsday ; that said, it also sounds like Stewart made good use of every moment he was onscreen. "He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who’s his best friend [Magneto], in the film," Russo explained. "It’s a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing."

It's also somewhat haunting to hear The Russos and Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige recall the almost prescient sense of finality both they and Stewart felt on his last day of filming. While no one knew it would be Patrick Stewart's final day ever on a film set – but somehow, they also kind of did .

“He stood up, and he gave a speech to the crew,” Kevin Feige shared. “We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.”

“I think it was in the back of all of our heads: we may never see him on set again,” Anthony Russo added, saying the whole experience was “Very emotional."

That emotion was only heightened by the fact that Patrick Stewart was already showing visible signs of poor health while filming Avengers: Doomsday . "It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew," Anthony Russo shared. "You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th.

articles.title: Steven Hack, Original ‘Cats’ Castmember and Busy Onscreen Character Actor, Dies at 68
articles.summary: His credits ranged from ‘Jake and the Fatman’ and ‘Seinfeld’ to ‘Pam & Tommy’ and ‘Amsterdam.’
articles.content:
Steven Hack, the theater veteran who spent five years on Broadway as an original castmember in Cats , then appeared as a character actor in dozens of films and TV shows, has died. He was 68.

Hack died Thursday at home following what was described as “a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the Interact Theatre Company announced . He was a founding member of the North Hollywood-based group that launched in 1989.

“Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family,” ITC directors Barry Heins and Walter Ware said in a statement. “His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle The Pulitzer-Winning Play 'Purpose' Finally Came to Los Angeles. But That Doesn't Mean It's Gone Hollywood. Lifestyle 'The Comedy About Spies' to Open on Broadway This Spring

Born in St. Louis on April 20, 1958, Hack studied at CalArts and The American Academy of Dramatic Arts in Los Angeles. In 1978, he was a background dancer in the film version of Grease and appeared in the off-Broadway musical The Coolest Cat in Town .

Hack was there when Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on Oct. 7, 1982, and he portrayed several characters, including Coricopat, Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Tumblebrutus and Pouncival, over the next five years.

He toured with Michael Bennett’s A Chorus Line for nearly two years and then joined the Broadway production at the Shubert Theatre for one show only — its record-breaking 3,389th Great White Way performance on Sept. 29, 1983. (He did Cats that night, too.)
